summary: Modern databases and data platforms have rapidly integrated native AI and ML capabilities, eliminating the need to move data to separate systems for inference, embedding generation, and vector search. By 2026, vector database adoption has grown 377% year over year, with 75% of enterprise AI applications depending on vector search capabilities, driving cloud data platforms like Snowflake, BigQuery, and Databricks to embed LLM integration, text-to-SQL, and semantic search directly into their query engines. The convergence of transactional, analytical, and vector workloads into unified platforms is reshaping enterprise AI architecture, with pgvector on PostgreSQL emerging as the lowest-friction path for teams already running Postgres infrastructure.

databases.name: Snowflake
databases.description: Snowflake Cortex AI provides a suite of serverless ML and LLM functions directly within the AI Data Cloud, including text-to-SQL, sentiment analysis, summarization, translation, and embedding generation. As of early 2026, Snowflake Postgres runs natively in the AI Data Cloud and integrates with Cortex AI functions, enabling vector similarity search via the pgvector extension alongside Cortex-powered embedding and text-to-SQL capabilities. Cortex Search and Cortex Analyst allow teams to build hybrid search pipelines and natural language interfaces over structured and unstructured data without moving data outside Snowflake.
databases.llm_integration: Native LLM functions via Cortex AI including models such as Mistral, LLaMA, and Snowflake Arctic; supports COMPLETE, EMBED, SUMMARIZE, SENTIMENT, and TRANSLATE functions; integrates with Snowflake Postgres and pgvector for vector similarity search; Cortex Analyst provides natural language to SQL generation
databases.pricing_notes: Cortex AI functions are billed by Snowflake credits consumed per token or per function call; embedding generation and LLM inference costs vary by model size and token volume; Snowflake Postgres pricing tied to compute credits; no separate licensing fee for Cortex functions beyond standard Snowflake consumption pricing

databases.name: Google BigQuery
databases.description: BigQuery ML allows data analysts and engineers to create and execute ML models directly using SQL inside BigQuery, supporting classification, regression, clustering, time series forecasting, and deep learning model training. BigQuery integrates natively with Vertex AI, enabling teams to call hosted foundation models and custom Vertex AI endpoints directly from SQL using the ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.EMBED_TEXT functions. BigQuery Vector Search extends this with approximate nearest neighbor search over embedding columns, enabling semantic search and RAG pipelines without extracting data from the warehouse.
databases.llm_integration: Native integration with Vertex AI foundation models including Gemini models via ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING SQL functions; supports remote model endpoints; BigQuery Studio provides a unified environment for SQL, Python notebooks, and Vertex AI model management; supports grounding and RAG patterns natively
databases.pricing_notes: BigQuery ML model training and inference billed per slot usage or on-demand per TB processed; ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING calls billed through Vertex AI at per-character or per-token rates depending on model; Vector Search index storage billed per GB per month; free tier includes 10 GB storage and 1 TB query processing per month

databases.name: PostgreSQL
databases.description: pgvector is an open-source PostgreSQL extension that adds vector data types and similarity search operators including L2 distance, inner product, and cosine distance, enabling semantic search, RAG pipelines, and recommendation systems without separate vector infrastructure. pgai is a complementary extension developed by Timescale that brings LLM functions directly into PostgreSQL, allowing embedding generation, summarization, and model inference calls via SQL against providers like OpenAI and Ollama. Together, pgvector and pgai make PostgreSQL a full-featured AI-ready database that requires no new infrastructure, reuses existing security models, and integrates with platforms like Snowflake and Databricks. For most teams, pgvector handles up to 50 million vectors effectively.
databases.llm_integration: pgai extension supports calling OpenAI, Ollama, Anthropic, and other LLM providers directly from SQL; Snowflake Postgres natively integrates pgvector with Cortex AI for embedding and text-to-SQL; Supabase and Timescale offer managed pgvector with built-in AI tooling; supports HNSW and IVFFlat indexing for approximate nearest neighbor search
databases.pricing_notes: pgvector and pgai are open-source and free to self-host on any PostgreSQL instance; managed offerings available through Supabase, Timescale, Neon, and AWS RDS with pricing based on compute and storage tiers; Snowflake Postgres billed via Snowflake credits; LLM API calls through pgai billed by the respective model provider such as OpenAI at standard token rates

databases.name: Amazon (Aurora ML + Redshift ML)
databases.description: Amazon Aurora ML integrates Aurora PostgreSQL and MySQL with Amazon SageMaker and Amazon Bedrock, allowing ML model inference to be called directly from SQL queries without data leaving the database; supported use cases include fraud detection, sentiment analysis, and custom model inference via SageMaker endpoints. Redshift ML enables data teams to create, train, and deploy ML models using SQL in Amazon Redshift, with automatic model training via SageMaker Autopilot and support for calling Bedrock foundation models for text generation and embedding tasks. Aurora PostgreSQL also supports the pgvector extension for native vector similarity search, enabling semantic search and RAG patterns within the existing RDS and Aurora infrastructure.
databases.llm_integration: Aurora ML integrates with Amazon Bedrock for foundation model inference including Anthropic Claude, Amazon Titan, and Meta LLaMA models callable via SQL functions; Redshift ML supports Bedrock model invocation and SageMaker Autopilot for automated training; pgvector supported on Aurora PostgreSQL for vector similarity search; Knowledge Bases for Amazon Bedrock can use Aurora as a vector store
databases.pricing_notes: Aurora ML and Redshift ML inference calls billed per invocation through SageMaker or Bedrock at standard API pricing; Bedrock charges per input and output token varying by model; pgvector on Aurora PostgreSQL incurs no additional licensing cost beyond standard Aurora instance pricing; Redshift ML training jobs billed through SageMaker compute time; data transfer costs may apply between services

databases.name: Databricks
databases.description: Databricks provides an end-to-end AI platform centered on Mosaic AI, which encompasses MLflow for experiment tracking and model lifecycle management, Model Serving for scalable LLM and custom model deployment, and Vector Search for managing and querying embedding indexes directly within the Databricks Lakehouse. DBRX is Databricks' own open-source mixture-of-experts foundation model available for fine-tuning and inference within the platform, complementing support for external models via the AI Gateway. Databricks Vector Search is a serverless similarity search engine built into Unity Catalog, enabling automatic synchronization of Delta Lake tables with embedding indexes for RAG pipelines, and integrates with pgvector-compatible workflows for teams migrating from Postgres.
databases.llm_integration: Supports DBRX, Meta LLaMA, Mistral, and external OpenAI-compatible models via Mosaic AI Model Serving and AI Gateway; MLflow Tracing provides observability for LLM applications; Databricks Vector Search integrates with LangChain, LlamaIndex, and other orchestration frameworks; supports fine-tuning foundation models on proprietary data using Mosaic AI Training; Unity Catalog governs model and embedding assets
databases.pricing_notes: Databricks billing based on Databricks Units (DBUs) consumed by compute clusters; Vector Search billed per DBU for index serving and sync compute; Model Serving billed per token for pay-per-token endpoints or per DBU for provisioned throughput; MLflow is open-source and free to self-host; DBRX model weights are open-source but inference costs apply when hosted on Databricks; pricing varies significantly by cloud provider and region

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas
databases.description: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search enables semantic search and RAG applications by storing vector embeddings alongside operational data in the same document database, eliminating synchronization complexity between transactional and vector stores. Atlas Vector Search supports approximate nearest neighbor search using HNSW indexing and allows pre-filtering by any MongoDB document fields, enabling highly targeted semantic retrieval without post-filtering overhead. Atlas integrates with major embedding providers and LLM frameworks including LangChain, LlamaIndex, and Amazon Bedrock, and is listed among the top enterprise vector database solutions for 2026 alongside Pinecone, Weaviate, and Qdrant.
databases.llm_integration: Integrates with OpenAI, Cohere, Hugging Face, and Amazon Bedrock for embedding generation; native connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex RAG pipelines; Atlas Stream Processing can trigger embedding generation on data changes; MongoDB Aggregation Pipeline allows combining vector search with metadata filtering and full-text search in a single query; supports multi-modal embeddings
databases.pricing_notes: Atlas Vector Search is included with MongoDB Atlas clusters at no additional per-feature cost; pricing based on Atlas cluster tier with shared free tier (M0) supporting limited vector search, and dedicated tiers starting from approximately $57 per month for M10; vector index storage counts toward cluster storage limits; costs scale with cluster size, storage, and data transfer; serverless Atlas instances also support vector search with consumption-based pricing
